title: Flight attendant for a day: At 84, Joyce Olson earns her wings
body_markdown:
As a former teacher, 84-year-old Joyce Olson spent her life inspiring others through her warmth, wisdom and quick wit. Yet, there was one dream that was never fulfilled: "I always wanted to be a flight attendant."


In fact, Joyce was hired as a flight attendant in the early 1960s, but circumstances beyond her control prevented her from flying. While her path ultimately led her to a rewarding career in education, the excitement and wonder of aviation never left her.


That’s when Lindsay Charlefour, Director of Life Enrichment – Waltonwood Communities and Platinum Medallion member, reached out to Delta’s Detroit (DTW) In-Flight Service (IFS) team. What followed was an extraordinary collaboration to help make Joyce’s dream a reality.


Led by Sarah Larson, Rel Smith, Mario Good, Michael Briggs, Tony Rogers, Finn Polakov and many others, the team transformed a simple wish into an unforgettable experience: a personalized "Flight Attendant for a Day" adventure at Detroit Metro Airport.


The celebration began before the big day, when Mario visited Joyce at Waltonwood to help make her feel comfortable and prepare her for what was to come. As a former teacher himself, Mario connected with Joyce immediately. Together, they walked through aspects of flight attendant training and practiced role-playing scenarios while her friends at Waltonwood acted as “customers.” Mario then answered questions about the job she’d dreamed about for so long.


### Finally, the day Joyce had been waiting for arrived.


Upon arriving at DTW, Joyce was welcomed as a member of the Delta team. She received her wings, proudly pinned on by her daughter, along with a custom Delta badge and her first assignment: a mock flight to Rome, one of the destinations she had always dreamed of visiting.


Joined by her daughter and son, who traveled from Salt Lake City and North Carolina, as well as an honorary son from Michigan, Joyce immersed herself in the experience. She participated in crew briefings, met pilots and flight attendants, learned about onboard operations and boarded an aircraft through Gate A5.


Family members and Delta leaders became her "customers," while Delta employees helped bring the experience to life.


### Throughout the day, Joyce's enthusiasm energized everyone around her.


"She had the crew having fun all day," Mario recalled. "She's optimistic, a great storyteller and someone who makes an impression immediately."


“The team took my request and elevated it at every turn, adding thoughtful Delta touches every step of the way,” said Lindsay. “I could go on and on about their teamwork, communication, elevation, kindness and collaboration. They changed Joyce’s life by their generosity and willingness to say ‘yes.’”


### For Mario and the DTW team, the goal was simple.


“We wanted Ms. Joyce to feel welcomed, celebrated and part of our Delta family,” said Mario. “For me, the joy was in connecting with Ms. Joyce and helping bring her dream to life. Being able to visit the senior citizen center and spend time with the residents was one of my richest moments. Honestly, it brought me as much joy as it brought them. That demographic is sometimes forgotten in our society. They matter, too, and it’s important to give back.”


The experience culminated with lunch, stories, laughter and a few surprises, including a signed commemorative photo, Delta memorabilia, a bouquet made from Biscoff cookies and a box of chocolates to mark the end of her international "journey."


As Joyce reflected on the day, she said she felt overwhelmed in the best possible way, grateful for the kindness shown by so many people who came together to make the experience special.


"As flight attendants, we have an opportunity to help people feel seen and valued both on and off the plane," Mario reflected. "That's what the Delta Spirit is all about."


Sometimes the most meaningful journeys aren't measured in miles, but in moments, connections and the people who make them unforgettable.


For one extraordinary day, Joyce's dream took flight, reminding everyone involved that it’s never too late.
